strings.ui.load: Build this algorithm in the application
strings.ui.offline: Open the classroom inside SimpleMotocam to load this sequence. The state and test image can also be downloaded.
strings.ui.intro: Each sequence targets OpenCV 2.4.13.7. Load it to inspect intermediate channels and change the mathematics. The examples are original teaching adaptations with source references.
strings.ui.bookNote: Local books are in D:\Dromation\Computer Vision. Page references distinguish printed pages from PDF pages; the books are not redistributed with the application.
strings.ui.codeNote: This Python orchestrator calls the genuine OpenCV 2.4 worker through SimpleMotocam. The C/C++/Java selector applies to the individual foundation lessons.
strings.ui.confirm: Replace the current algorithm with this OpenCV 2.4 exercise and its test scene?
strings.ui.legacyCode: OpenCV 2.4 custom Python: use NumPy for algebra and cv24.run(kind, plane, **parameters) for native operations. Importing cv2 refers to this limited bridge, never silently to OpenCV 4.
strings.red-part.title: Find a red part
strings.red-part.goal: Select a red object against a neutral or green background. The output is a binary mask of sufficiently large red regions.
strings.red-part.order: Extract the color channels, subtract green from red, then threshold. Opening removes isolated foreground pixels before component filtering measures the remaining connected regions.
strings.red-part.tune: Start with threshold 0.20, opening size 3 and minimum area 100 pixels. Raise the threshold to reject weak redness; raise the area limit to reject small fragments.
strings.red-part.expected: The supplied scene contains one large red rectangle, a green rectangle and small red specks. The final mask should keep only the large red rectangle.
strings.red-part.caution: This is color segmentation, not object recognition. White balance, colored illumination and highlights change the difference. The threshold uses normalized float channels.
strings.bright-regions.title: Keep large bright regions
strings.bright-regions.goal: Separate bright parts from a dark background and reject tiny regions by their actual pixel area.
strings.bright-regions.order: Convert RGB to luminance, smooth small fluctuations, threshold, then filter connected regions. Area filtering comes after segmentation because it needs a binary foreground.
strings.bright-regions.tune: Use Gaussian size 3 and sigma 1, threshold 0.60 and minimum area 80. Compare the threshold output with the final mask while raising the area limit.
strings.bright-regions.expected: Two large bright parts remain. A dark hole inside a part stays a hole; it does not contribute to the foreground area. Tiny bright dots disappear.
strings.bright-regions.caution: Eight-connectivity joins pixels touching at a corner. Touching physical objects can therefore become one region. Pixel area is not a calibrated physical area.
strings.motion.title: Detect changes between frames
strings.motion.goal: Find regions whose color changed between consecutive frames from a fixed camera.
strings.motion.order: Keep signed channel differences, combine their magnitudes, threshold, remove isolated pixels, then reject small regions. A second frame is required before a difference exists.
strings.motion.tune: Start with magnitude threshold 0.12, opening size 3 and minimum area 40. Step through two frames, then compare the signed red difference with the magnitude and mask.
strings.motion.expected: The first processed frame is empty. Later frames show changed portions around the moving synthetic part, including its previous location.
strings.motion.caution: This detects change, not identity or a full object silhouette. Camera motion, flicker and shadows also produce responses. Restarting the algorithm resets the previous frame.
strings.lines.title: Detect straight edges
strings.lines.goal: Turn a grayscale edge map into a mask of long straight line segments.
strings.lines.order: Compute luminance and smooth it before Canny. Hough then groups edge pixels into candidate line segments. Thresholding a color region is a different task from finding its boundary.
strings.lines.tune: Use Gaussian size 3, Canny low 40 and high 100, Hough votes 30, minimum length 60 and maximum gap 5. Canny thresholds are in the quantized 8-bit gradient domain.
strings.lines.expected: Long straight features are retained while short isolated marks are rejected. A thick bright stripe may produce two boundary lines.
strings.lines.caution: A line mask is not a fitted physical dimension. Perspective, calibration and uncertainty must be addressed before metrology. More votes do not guarantee a more accurate line.
strings.edges.title: Find edges after suppressing noise
strings.edges.goal: Compare impulsive noise with coherent object boundaries using median filtering and a Laplacian response.
strings.edges.order: Convert to luminance, apply a small median filter, compute the signed Laplacian, take its absolute value, then threshold. Absolute value keeps both edge polarities.
strings.edges.tune: Start with median size 3 and response threshold 0.15. Inspect the signed Laplacian before the absolute-value block. Increase the median size to compare lost fine detail.
strings.edges.expected: Sparse salt-and-pepper pixels mostly disappear, while the rectangle boundary remains. This is a detection adaptation, not a copy of the book’s artistic outlining effect.
strings.edges.caution: The Laplacian amplifies residual noise. Filtering can erase thin objects. This exercise uses float32, a size-3 median and a size-1 Laplacian stencil, unlike the book’s color effect.
strings.uneven-light.title: Segment under uneven illumination
strings.uneven-light.goal: Extract dark marks on a slowly varying bright background using a local threshold.
strings.uneven-light.order: Convert to luminance, smooth, use adaptive Gaussian thresholding, invert the result, then remove small regions. Inversion makes the dark marks the foreground.
strings.uneven-light.tune: Start with adaptive window size 15, offset 5 and minimum area 50. The window must be odd and wider than the mark. The offset is in 8-bit intensity units.
strings.uneven-light.expected: The two dark bars remain across the brightness gradient. Compare with a fixed threshold to see why the locally estimated background helps.
strings.uneven-light.caution: A window that is too small can detect only outlines or miss wide marks. Strong texture and sharp shadows can resemble defects. This is an illustrative inspection task, not a trained defect classifier.
